findings.summary: Skua achieved a higher held-out success rate than Plover-PG (44.63% vs 40.50%), a statistically significant improvement (paired t-test, p=0.0029, 95% CI [1.82, 6.44] percentage points).
findings.scope: 200 held-out Mirefield levels, 10 seeds, primary endpoint success rate
findings.caveats: Only this dataset and setting; no general claim beyond Mirefield.

findings.summary: Skua's normalized return (62.95) was not significantly different from Plover-PG's (62.04) (paired t-test, p=0.27, 95% CI [-0.84, 2.66]).
findings.scope: 200 held-out Mirefield levels, 10 seeds, secondary endpoint normalized return
findings.caveats: Non-significance does not imply equivalence; CI includes both negative and positive differences.

findings.summary: The Tally bonus reference agent (success 42.10%, return 62.71) performed between Plover-PG and Skua on both metrics, but no statistical tests were reported for comparisons involving it.

sentences.text: On the 200 held-out Mirefield levels, Skua achieved a significantly higher success rate than Plover-PG (44.63% vs 40.50%; paired t-test, p = 0.0029, 95% CI [1.82, 6.44] percentage points).

However, the difference in normalized return was not statistically significant (62.95 vs 62.04; paired t-test, p = 0.27, 95% CI [-0.84, 2.66]), and this non-significance does not establish equivalence.
The reference agent with the Tally bonus scored between the two on both metrics (success 42.10%, return 62.71), but no statistical tests were reported for comparisons involving it.
